aspect: Abroad, the identity is a filter applied by other people
description: Some partners and their families treat the nationality as a political complication, a security concern, or a visa liability, and withdraw on those grounds without ever naming them. The pattern is felt long before it can be articulated.
energy_note: Ended for reasons nobody will put in a sentence.

aspect: Being used and discarded is a specific, reported pattern
description: Relationships in which the Palestinian partner is a novelty, a political accessory or a cause rather than a person - intense, admiring, and ended when the cost of association becomes real. The brief names this and it belongs here: the harm is that the interest was never in you.
energy_note: Fascinating for a season, and then expensive.

aspect: At home, the document decides who is marriageable
description: The ID tiers convert marriage into an immigration calculation. A green ID marrying a blue ID means a family unification file; marrying a Gaza ID means separation. Families factor this in openly, and people are rejected for their paperwork.
energy_note: Turned down for the colour of your card.
notes: See FAM-001 and IDR-002 for the mechanism this is downstream of.

aspect: Unmarried women carry a specific stigma
description: Research on 'spinsterhood' in Palestine finds the societal expectation of marriage marginalises women who fall outside it, and that the number of unmarried women can become a locus of moral panic - in a society already under prolonged insecure and warlike conditions. The same work finds a long tradition of unmarried women leading full lives, which is the part that never gets quoted.
energy_note: A demographic statistic, experienced as a personal failing.

aspect: Widows and divorced women face a narrower market and lose custody either way
description: In Gaza, widows and divorced women historically had two options: marry a divorced or widowed man, or remain alone. Custody compounds it - when a divorced woman remarries her former husband tends to get the children; when a widow remarries her children tend to go to her late husband's family.
energy_note: Remarry and lose the children. Don't, and be alone.

aspect: Remarriage after martyrdom is sometimes about the children, not the widow
description: Norms shifted after the first intifada so that previously unmarried men may marry martyrs' widows - reportedly often less for the widow's welfare than to secure custody of her children.

aspect: The prisoner's wife is a category with no name and no end
description: Married to a man serving decades, she is neither married in practice nor free to remarry, running the household alone and the prison administration on top of it, indefinitely.

aspect: And the isolation removes the thing that buffers everything else
description: Partnership is the single largest protective factor against every stressor in this dataset. A market distorted by documents, politics and stigma removes it precisely from the people carrying the most.
energy_note: The main shock absorber, priced out of reach.

aspect: EXAMPLE - custody as the mechanism, not a side effect
description: In Gaza, when a divorced woman remarries her former husband tends to get custody of the children; when a widow remarries, her children tend to be cared for by her late husband's family. Norms shifted after the first intifada so previously unmarried men may marry martyrs' widows - reportedly often to secure custody of the children rather than for the widow's welfare.
energy_note: Remarry, and the children go elsewhere.
